audit_findings.title: Parent-share denominator may be paired with consolidated owner-earnings components
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 noncontrolling-interest earnings $337 million; 2025 NCI claims $1.893 billion including redeemable NCI; exact parent allocation unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated cash-flow add-backs, maintenance capex, and cash may enter OE or the bridge while value is divided by parent-only diluted shares.
audit_findings.evidence: For our consolidated non-wholly owned subsidiaries, a noncontrolling interest is recognized to reflect the portion of income and equity that is not attributable to us.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates material minority ownership, but the supplied record does not demonstrate that the valuation actually failed to allocate each consolidated component. NCI earnings equal 4.9% of the $6.8797 billion anchor, while the minority share of cash, capex, and other OE adjustments is not disclosed here, so the valuation effect could be meaningful but cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Trace every 2025 OE component and the June 2026 cash/STI balance between parent and NCI claims, then rerun all scenarios using parent-attributable OE and bridge assets only.

audit_findings.title: Non-service pension income may be treated as recurring distributable earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 pre-tax non-service pension income $1.182 billion; 2026 first-half income $703 million; exact after-tax OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, non-cash expected asset returns and actuarial pension components inflate normalized OE and therefore every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Net periodic benefit (income) expense is classified between operating and non-operating, whereby only the service cost component is included in operating profit and the remaining components are included in Non-service pension income.
audit_findings.explanation: The pension income is demonstrated in the filed income statement and is large relative to the $6.8797 billion OE anchor. What remains unresolved is whether the OE calculation purged it. Because the disclosed method identifies only an interest-income purge, retaining even a substantial portion is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Provide the OE reconciliation, remove all non-service pension components, substitute normalized service cost and required parent cash contributions without double counting, and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Recurring commercial-aerospace investment may escape both earnings and capex deductions
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 intangible-investment cash outflow $492 million, equal to 7.2% of anchor OE; remaining net exclusivity commitments $5.5 billion; 2026 first-half outflow $156 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized exclusivity and collaboration payments can avoid current earnings expense and property-capex deductions, while related amortization may be added back in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, our exclusivity assets, net of accumulated amortization, were approximately $3.7 billion, and our remaining estimated commitments, net of collaborator share, were approximately $5.5 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash investments and commitments are demonstrated, but their treatment in OE and the maintenance-versus-growth allocation are unresolved. The 2025 outflow alone is meaningful relative to anchor OE, and the multi-year commitments establish enough scale for a missing normalized deduction to materially overstate operating and terminal value. The full $5.5 billion should not automatically be deducted because timing and economic classification remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE to investing cash flows and intangible amortization, separate acquired-intangible amortization from internally funded platform assets, classify maintenance versus growth investment, and rerun with a normalized recurring deduction or explicit commitment schedule.

audit_findings.title: Powder-metal cash costs can disappear because the charge and payment occur in different years
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 accrual utilization $1.0 billion, equal to 14.5% of anchor OE; estimated 2026 cash impact $700 million; June 2026 remaining customer-compensation accrual $400 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Payments and customer credits reduce an accrued liability rather than current earnings, so an earnings-based anchor can omit the owner cost when the original 2023 provision is outside the accepted OE series.
audit_findings.evidence: In both 2025 and 2024, we utilized $1.0 billion of the accrual through cash payments and credits issued to customers.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge-payment timing mismatch and current-period utilization are demonstrated; whether OE separately captured them is unresolved. The 2025 and expected 2026 amounts are large relative to anchor OE, making the issue capable of materially changing the normalized anchor. Any correction must avoid deducting both the 2023 provision and subsequent utilization.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct the 2023-2026 liability roll-forward, cash payments, customer credits, partner recoveries, and EAC effects; establish one normalized parent-share economic charge and rerun the OE series without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Large unaccrued government claims are absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 gross asserted claims and stated interest total $6.126 billion, equal to $4.43 per diluted share and 6.1% of base equity value; probability-weighted exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any genuinely unrecognized expected settlement is a claim senior to common equity and should reduce the equity bridge; related recurring interest or legal costs may also affect OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As previously disclosed, in April 2019, a Divisional Administrative Contracting Officer (DACO) of the United States DCMA asserted a claim against Pratt & Whitney to recover alleged overpayments of approximately $1.7 billion plus interest ($1.5 billion at December 31, 2025).
audit_findings.explanation: The asserted amounts and ongoing litigation are demonstrated, but they are disputed, some rulings have favored RTX, and the record does not establish the accrued, escrowed, recoverable, or probable loss amount. The gross exposure is large enough to matter, but it is not a valid valuation deduction without probability and recognition evidence.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest accrual and escrow balances by claim, counsel-supported outcome ranges, recovery rights, and procedural updates; deduct only the probability-weighted unrecognized parent liability and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: 2025 disposal gains and sold-business earnings may contaminate a no-perimeter-adjustment anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 pre-tax disposal gains $300 million, equal to 4.4% of anchor OE before tax; 2025 disposition proceeds $1.931 billion; sold-business OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: One-time gains and partial-year earnings from disposed operations can inflate anchor OE, while sale proceeds remaining in cash are separately added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The sale resulted in a pre-tax gain of $0.2 billion, which was recorded in Other income (expense), net within the Consolidated Statement of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The $300 million of gains and the dispositions are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the gains were purged or quantify the sold businesses' parent-attributable OE and maintenance investment. The identified gains alone are below 5% of the anchor before tax, but unquantified sold-business earnings and the absent perimeter adjustment prevent a supported not-material conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Produce a 2025 continuing-perimeter OE reconciliation removing both disposal gains and disposed-business earnings and maintenance investment, verify proceeds enter value only through cash, and rerun the trend anchor and scenarios.
